reports.title: Energizer Holdings, Inc. Announces Fiscal 2026 Fourth Quarter and Full Year Results

guidance.heading: Fiscal 2027 Outlook
section: •Organic Net Sales expected to be flat to down low single digits, reflecting portfolio actions focused on durable margins and cash generation
•Adjusted EBITDA expected to grow approximately 5% to 9%, excluding fiscal 2026 tariff refund
•Free Cash Flow expected to increase more than 30% to approximately $300 million, enabling shareholder dividends and meaningful debt reduction
St. Louis —November 17, 2026—Energizer Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: ENR) today announced results for the fourth fiscal quarter and full fiscal year, which ended September 30, 2026.

"Energizer delivered a strong finish to fiscal 2026, with improved margins, higher earnings and substantial free cash flow generation in the fourth quarter,” said Mark LaVigne, Chief Executive Officer. “The work completed through Project Momentum has strengthened our operating model and created a solid foundation for the future. We expect to leverage that foundation to drive a meaningful step-up in free cash flow, providing greater capacity to invest behind our brands, reduce debt and return capital to shareholders.”

desk.headline: Sales down 4.8% to $793.2m, in line; adjusted EPS up 30% to $1.37, beat; fiscal 2027 outlook of $560–580m adjusted EBITDA and ~$300m free cash flow
results: Sales fell 4.8% to $793.2m, mostly because a licensed battery brand from the APS deal has ended; on an organic basis sales slipped only 0.6%.
Batteries & Lights grew about 1.5% organically on new distribution and online sales, while Auto Care fell as refrigerant shipments were pulled into the prior quarter.
Profitability jumped: adjusted gross margin rose 4 points to 42.5%, adjusted EPS rose 30% to $1.37 and GAAP EPS nearly doubled to $0.99.
Strong cash quarter: free cash flow of $123.6m allowed $85.7m of debt to be repaid; for the year free cash flow more than tripled to $228.6m and debt fell $167.7m.
Full year: sales flat at $2.95bn, adjusted EPS $3.37 (vs $3.52); the Project Momentum cost programme is complete after about $230m of savings.

guidance.summary: First outlook for fiscal 2027 (to Sep 2027): organic sales flat to down low single digits as it drops about $25m of low-margin business, adjusted EBITDA of $560–580m (5–9% growth excluding this year's $64m tariff refund) and free cash flow of about $300m. No EPS guidance was given.

items.new: flat to down low single digits

points: Management's plan is simple: protect margins, generate cash and pay down debt, with spare cash after the dividend going to debt reduction.

It expects 200–300 basis points of cost pressure in fiscal 2027, mainly zinc, steel, energy and freight, to be offset by savings, factory efficiencies and targeted price rises; gross margin is aimed at about 40% or a bit higher.
The plan assumes battery category sales keep falling about 1.5%, though recent weeks have been better and Energizer says it is gaining share.
US promotions are slightly elevated and shoppers are showing more interest in private label; exiting private-label refrigerant work will weigh on Auto Care sales.
Cash should rise as restructuring spending largely ends, capital spending normalises and delayed tax-credit cash of about $45m arrives.
